BiblicalUsage: Yahălôm is a precious stone set in the breastpiece of the high priest, in the second row beside the emerald and the sapphire. Ezekiel names it among the stones that covered the king of Tyre in Eden, a picture of beauty given and then lost.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that God delights in beauty made to last, and a stone set in gold on the breastpiece says the tribes are carried close to His heart.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
